name.text: Determinig Order of Rotational Symmetry of polygons

questiontext.text:
(a) What is the order of rotational symmetry of the shape shown below?

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

(a) Order of rotational symmetry

The order of rotational symmetry is the number of times a shape fits exactly onto itself during one complete turn of \(360^\circ\).

The shape shown is a {@shape_name@}.

It matches itself {@order_sym@} time(s) during one full rotation.

Therefore, the order of rotational symmetry is \[ \boxed{{@order_sym@}} \]

(b) Smallest angle of rotation

The smallest angle of rotation is found by dividing a full turn by the order of rotational symmetry.

If a shape has rotational symmetry of order \(n\), then the smallest angle through which it can be rotated to coincide with itself is \[ \frac{360^\circ}{n}. \]

\[ \text{Smallest angle} = \frac{360^\circ}{{@order_sym@}} = {@ta_angle@}^\circ \]

Therefore, the smallest angle of rotation is \[ \boxed{{@ta_angle@}^\circ} \]
